title: Who's Who: Jonas Calder
summary: Alderwick civic engineer whose work remains part of the record of modern Eidetics.
author: Who's Who Desk
paragraphs: The Correspondent adds Jonas Calder (1827–1879) to its Who's Who of Eideticians, recording a alderwick civic engineer whose name still attends serious discussion of the Eidetic Stratum.

Calder supervised the receiving hall opened in 1868, placing instrument rooms, public galleries, and a controlled expedition chamber under one roof. Its daily bulletins made Eidetic measurements part of civic life.
He died convinced that open observation, even of unwelcome readings, was the hall’s most valuable safeguard.

For Alderwick readers, Jonas Calder is remembered not as an ornament to legend but as a figure whose work helps explain why Eideticians prize careful terms, repeatable evidence and a sober account of what remains unknown.
